answer: A real estate investment trust (REIT) is a company that owns and typically operates income-producing real estate or related assets, such as apartments, offices, or warehouses. REITs give individuals a way to earn a share of income from commercial real estate without buying the property themselves. Many REITs are publicly traded, while others are not; that distinction can affect how readily shares can be sold and how easily their value can be assessed.
